reasons: clang/lib/CodeGen/CGBuiltin.cpp:23254 (EmitPULPBuiltinShuffle, generic run-time-mask path): Builder.CreateZExt(mask lane, Int32Ty) is an invalid cast when the mask lanes are wider than 32 bits, so clang hits the assertion 'Illegal ZExt' (ZExtInst ctor) on valid GCC code on riscv32. Reproducer logs/20-F019-review/q2.c: typedef long long v2l __attribute__((vector_size(16))); v2l f(v2l a, v2l m){ return __builtin_shuffle(a,m); } (and the same with a v2d double vector and a v2l mask, 3-argument form). GAP9 GCC compiles both. Sema accepts them (64-bit mask lanes for 64-bit vector lanes is a legal GCC shape), so this is a crash reachable from code the note says is supported ('correct for any vector'). The worker's GVSoC matrix and proposed tests never cover lanes wider than 16 bits. Fix: take the index modulo NumSrcElts in the mask lane's own type and then zext-or-trunc (or zext-or-trunc to i64 first). Watch the i8 case where 2N can be 256.

clang/lib/CodeGen/CGBuiltin.cpp:23216 (constant-mask path): APSInt::getZExtValue() asserts ('Too many bits for uint64_t') for a negative constant in a 128-bit mask lane. Reproducer logs/20-F019-review/q.c on riscv64 (the builtin has no feature gate, so it exists on every RISC-V target): typedef __int128 v2q __attribute__((vector_size(32))); __builtin_shuffle(a,(v2q){-1,2}). Use APInt::urem(NumSrcElts) or read only the low bits. This matters less than the first reason (no rv32 exposure), but it is the same one-line kind of fix in the same function and should come with it.

Also needed in the resubmission: add a >32-bit lane shape (for example v2l/v2d, run-time and constant mask) to proposed_test and to the GVSoC generator, so the generic path is exercised for every lane width Sema accepts.

Upstream-File-Edit (CGBuiltin.cpp, which the fork did not touch before): accepted in principle. At llvmorg-20.1.8, EmitRISCVBuiltinExpr is where every RISC-V CustomTypeChecking builtin is lowered (ntl_load/ntl_store, BuiltinsRISCV.td:145). The fork's other __builtin_pulp_* builtins lower through ClangBuiltin intrinsic mapping, which cannot express polymorphic operand types plus a constant-vs-run-time split. Every alternative I could find is worse. A Sema rewrite into ShuffleVectorExpr also needs upstream SemaChecking and does not cover the 3-argument run-time form. A macro in a fork header over the 2-operand __builtin_shufflevector(v, mask) form needs a forced include and cannot build the 0..2N-1 concat list without knowing N. The hunk is one static function plus a 2-line dispatch. Carry-forward cost: from llvm 21 on, RISC-V builtin codegen lives in clang/lib/CodeGen/TargetBuiltins/RISCV.cpp, so the hunk will have to move there. SemaRISCV.cpp, BuiltinsRISCVXpulp.td and DiagnosticSemaKinds.td are files the fork already owns or touches, so nothing is edited in SemaChecking.cpp.
Scope note, acceptable: with no feature gate, __has_builtin(__builtin_shuffle) is now true on every RISC-V target. This matches GCC and matches the note's stated intent.

Sema vs GCC: I ran my own logs/20-F019-review/d.c against clang 20-F019 and GAP9 GCC 7.1.1. Non-vector, mismatched vector types (v4s vs v4u), lane count, non-integer mask, lane size, 1 argument, 4 arguments and a wrong result type are rejected by both, 1:1. v4u with a v4s mask and v2f with a v2i mask are accepted by both.

Constant masks: the IR is shufflevector with indices = zext(mask) mod N/2N. For example (v4s){9,-1,15,6} gives <1,3,3,2> for one vector and <1,7,7,6> for two, matching GCC's modulo rule, also at -O0 (-disable-llvm-passes). A mask with side effects correctly takes the run-time path. Run-time masks with +xpulpv on v4i8/v2i16 (also v2 x _Float16 via bitcast) become llvm.riscv.pulp.shuffleb/shuffleh/shuffle4b/shuffle2h with v1 as the rD operand. The Pat maps intrinsic operand 0 to PV_SHUFFLE2_* $rd. Without Xpulpv, or for other shapes, the result is an extract/urem/insert sequence that the optimiser reduces to 'and 2N-1'.

ISel change (3230522cc545): llc -mattr=+xpulpv -verify-machineinstrs (logs/20-F019-review/s.ll) on two-vector v4i8 <0,4,1,5> gives lui/addi 0x05010400 + pv.shuffle2.b a0,a1,a2. v4i8 with an undef lane, v2i16 <1,2> (0x00020001 + pv.shuffle2.h) and <8 x i8> split into two pv.shuffle2.b all produce selectors I checked by hand, including the 8x8 case's operand choice. build/int-20 llc asserts on the same file ('Value is not an N-bit signed value'), which confirms the worker's crash-before claim. GVSoC defect confirmed from source. gvsoc2/core/models/cpu/iss/include/isa_lib/int.h:949-966 lib_VEC_SHUFFLE2_16/8 switch source order on #ifdef RISCV. The old ISS adds -DRISCV=1 (core/models/cpu/iss/riscv.py:206, CMakeLists.txt:78), while iss_v2/riscv.py (used by ri5ky_testbench) never does. Format_RRRR (isa_gen/isa_pulpv2.py) binds a=rs1, b=rs2, c=rD, so the RISCV branch means 'selector bit set -> rs1, clear -> rD'. That is the RI5CY/CV32E40P ISA definition of pv.shuffle2/cv.shuffle2. The worker's semantics (v1 in rD = lanes 0..N-1, v2 in rs1 = lanes N..2N-1) match the ISA, not just the patched simulator. The patch is the minimal #if 1 on those two functions.

My own GVSoC test (logs/20-F019-review/t3.c + run.sh, scalar reference through unions): one- and two-vector constant masks with out-of-range and negative indices on v4s/v4u/v2s/v2u; 8x8, 4x16 and 2x32 generic shapes; the SDK-style local-variable mask; 200 random run-time masks per shape. On the patched GVSoC, clang has 0 mismatches for xpulpv2 -O2/-O0 and generic -O2/-O0. On stock GVSoC, the two-vector pv.shuffle2 groups fail for clang-xpulpv2 and GCC alike, and the generic builds pass, as the worker reported. GCC fails c1-2 (2/10) and c2-2 (1/10) on the patched simulator.

GCC pv.shuffle.sci.h claim: I confirmed the encoding. GCC emits 0xc2876757 'pv.shuffle.sci.h a4,a4,17' for a lane-1 broadcast, which sets instr[25] and instr[23]. Both ISSes read the lane-0/1 selectors from imm6 bits 0/1 (Format_RRU imm = {instr[24:20], instr[25]}; getShuffleHalfSci). To my knowledge the RI5CY/CV32E40P decoder uses instr[25]/instr[20] too (imm_shuffleh_type), and the fork's LLVM agrees. So GCC's lane-1 selector sits in the wrong bit, and it works only for masks like {1,0} where that bit happens not to matter. The worker's 'confirm on silicon' hedge is appropriate. The fork's LLVM sci.h ISel is unchanged by this branch.
